- No new hardware needed if you have a tablet or computer in the kitchen.

# Waste Tracker: Kitchen Setup Plan (one page)

**Time the kitchen spends: about 6-8 minutes per shift, all outside service hours.**

## What kitchen staff do each shift
1. Before close (about 3 min): weigh or count discarded food, pick the item and reason from a short list on a tablet or clipboard (spoiled, overprep, plate waste, dropped).
2. After close (about 3-5 min): review the day's entries on one screen, correct any mistakes, and submit.

## What the owner gets
- Weekly totals by item and reason, sent each Monday.
- A short list of the top 3 items to cut.

## Setup (one time, about 1 hour)
- I install the tracker on one tablet or existing computer and set up the item list with your chef.
- I train the staff on-site in one 30-minute session.
- Two-week trial, then we review together.

## Cost

Week 52. Fernway still covers my costs, so I'm not in crisis. But this year I mostly waited: on my parents for names, on intros that went quiet, on a pilot that kept slipping. The cold-email plan never happened because I couldn't reach restaurant owners with the tools I had. The tracker went to Builders Forum, where the criticism was sharp and useful. I put it on hold at week 44.

What I've learned is that I can't build a pilot while waiting for permission from people outside my week. The next step has to be something I can do alone, even if it's small.

Next quarter I'll keep the Fernway job, apply to a few roles each week, and pick one pilot task that doesn't depend on anyone else's reply. At week 60 I'll look at real numbers, not hopes.
